column1: # PostgreSQL-style SQL prototype: the answer parity corpus (issue #2).
# Columns, separated by one TAB: id, order, tol, status, statement, expected.

# id: unique, lower case, words joined by hyphens. Add a case at the end of its group; never renumber or reuse an id. An id that starts with err- is a statement the server must refuse: its expected is the SQLSTATE and the engine must refuse it with the same SQLSTATE.

# order: ordered when the statement has an ORDER BY that is a total order on its rows (row order is then part of the answer), multiset otherwise (the same rows the same number of times, in any order). Stated for every statement.

# tol: - for the default floating point tolerance (1e-9, relative to the larger of 1 and the two values) or a number. Only floating point values use it: integers, numeric and text compare exactly, numbers by value (38.5 equals 38.50).

# status: ok = the engine is expected to answer like the server. pending = the engine does not support the statement yet: the harness runs it on the server only for its outcome, tries it on the engine, and reports it as pending, never as failed. When the engine answers a pending statement like the server the run fails until the flag is flipped to ok.
# statement: one statement, with backslash, tab, line feed and carriage return written as \\, \t, \n and \r.

# expected: written by the generator from the real server, never by hand: {"columns":[labels],"types":[PostgreSQL type names],"rows":[[cells]]}, or {"error":"SQLSTATE"}. Cells: NULL is null, numbers are numbers, text is text, dates and timestamps are ISO text, arrays are JSON arrays, jsonb is JSON. pending-server = the generator has not run on the case yet: add a case with that value, then run the generator.
# rules of the comparison: the classes Values and ResultComparator in com.arcadedb.query.postgresql.corpus.
# data: the small fixture of issue #2, engine/src/test/resources/postgresql/small-schema.sql loaded into PostgreSQL and SmallFixture built in ArcadeDB.

# ids in expected: the record ids of the fixture file (#<table number>:<row number>, as small-schema.sql numbers them), not ArcadeDB's real record ids, which depend on the buckets of a type. The harness translates the engine's real record ids to the file's before it compares (ArcadeSide.setRidAliases); a test of the engine tree does the same.
# generator: see the header of syntax.tsv.
# server: PostgreSQL 18.7 (Debian 18.7-1.pgdg13+5) on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit
